record.paper_title: Open Problems in Engineering and Quality Assurance of Safety Critical Machine Learning Systems
record.context_brief: Extending safety assurance notations for ML uncertainty
record.original_question: How should system-level assurance methods such as STAMP/STPA and Goal Structuring Notation be extended so that they can express uncertainty related to machine-learning models in safety-critical subsystems?

evidence.quote: System-level technologies STAMP/STPA [16] and GSN [17] have received attention in recent years. They are highly promising, but they will need an extension that can express the uncertainty related to the machine-learning models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider two system-level safety assurance frameworks used for engineering safety-critical systems:

1. STAMP/STPA (Systems-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes / System-Theoretic Process Analysis): a hazard analysis technique that models a system as a hierarchical control structure of controllers, actuators, sensors, and controlled processes, and identifies unsafe control actions and their causal scenarios.

2. Goal Structuring Notation (GSN): a graphical argumentation notation for safety cases, in which top-level safety goals are decomposed via strategies into subgoals, supported by context, assumptions, justifications, and evidence (solutions).

Now consider safety-critical systems that contain subsystems implemented by machine-learning models, i.e., functions f: X → Y obtained by training on data, whose behavior carries intrinsic uncertainty (epistemic uncertainty about the learned hypothesis, aleatoric uncertainty in the data and operating environment, distributional shift between training and deployment, and quantifiable confidence/calibration of predictions).

Problem. Propose a principled extension of STAMP/STPA and of GSN such that:
(a) STAMP/STPA control-structure models and unsafe-control-action / causal-scenario analyses can explicitly represent and reason about machine-learning–induced uncertainty (e.g., model confidence, input-distribution coverage, training-data assumptions, and failure modes specific to learned components);
(b) GSN safety-case arguments can express claims, strategies, contexts, assumptions, and evidence types that capture and discharge machine-learning uncertainty in a sound, auditable manner;
(c) The extensions admit a formal semantics or notational discipline that supports compositional reasoning when learned components are integrated into the broader control system.

Provide such extensions, including their syntax, semantics, and demonstration that they faithfully capture the uncertainty associated with ML components in safety-critical subsystems.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of extending STAMP/STPA and GSN to capture machine-learning uncertainty has received active attention since 2018, with multiple proposed extensions (e.g., assurance-case patterns for ML, AMLAS methodology, STPA variants for ML-enabled systems), but no single, agreed-upon, formally complete extension has emerged. The general problem remains open as a research area.

status_evidence.title: Assurance of Machine Learning in Autonomous Systems (AMLAS)
status_evidence.snippet: AMLAS provides a methodology and GSN-based assurance case patterns for machine learning components, indicating ongoing work rather than a closed solution.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions of GSN for ML assurance are an active, ongoing research effort.

status_evidence.title: STPA for ML-enabled systems (survey literature)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work proposes adaptations of STPA to systems containing learned components, but acknowledges open challenges regarding uncertainty representation.
status_evidence.claim: STPA extensions for ML uncertainty are proposed but not definitive.
